findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Bullet B downgrades an unresolved earlier major to minor whenever the planner left that part unchanged, so an ignored finding no longer forces a round
findings.evidence: Bullet B: 'From round 2, raise a major only on a part the brief lists as changed or new, or on a defect earlier rounds missed ...; otherwise minor, even where a rule above says major.' An earlier major that the planner did not address sits on an unchanged part and was raised before, so it is not 'missed'. Bullet B therefore makes it minor. Bullet A ('name any that was not') sets no severity. plan_verdict (planning.rs:426) accepts when the critic accepts and no finding is blocker or major, so a plan that ignores an earlier major can now be accepted. The request asks the critic to 'check that those findings were resolved'. The criterion 3 pin test checks only phrases, so it would not catch this. Fix: In bullet A, say an unresolved earlier finding is raised again at its earlier severity, for example: '...; raise any that was not again at its earlier severity.' In bullet B, write 'raise a new major only on ...' so it limits new findings only. Re-count the bytes (about 30 more; the plan's own ceiling of 461 still allows it). Add 'again at its earlier severity' and 'a new major only' to the phrases the criterion 3 pin test asserts. Update D189 and the changelog to say so.
findings.location: Decision 2 / Step 5 (critic.md bullets A and B); Demonstration for criterion 3

findings.summary: The approach is one free-text paragraph that nearly every revision rewrites, so 'Approach' will almost always be listed as changed. That weakens the 'changed parts only' limit, because most majors can be tied to the approach.
findings.evidence: plan_body prints 'Approach: {approach}' as a single item (briefs/plan.rs:52). The plan compares it as one exact-text item. The plan's own demonstrations expect 'Changed or new: Approach' in every round. Fix: Either say in bullet B or the brief's intro that a changed approach alone does not make every unchanged decision, file, step or demonstration 'changed', or state this weakening as a known limit in D189's Tradeoff.

findings.summary: The digest is only an oracle if the producer records it from the unmodified code. The verifier sees only the final tree and cannot confirm the literal was not taken after the edit.
findings.evidence: Step 1 has the producer read the digest from a failing run before editing planner.rs. The cut-equality assertion only shows the brief with history equals the brief without history plus the new section. Both briefs could have drifted together. Fix: Have the producer report the digest it recorded before the edit together with the command output, so the verifier can match it. Or also add a few exact-line assertions on the tail (the heading order and the 'End with the critique' line) that do not depend on the step order.

findings.summary: 'revising_critique() with summary F1' is ambiguous: the critique's summary is not printed in the brief, only the findings are.
findings.evidence: revising_critique (tests.rs:1295-1309) has a critique-level 'summary' and a finding-level 'summary'. findings_list (briefs/plan.rs:28-46) prints only the finding fields. If the producer sets the critique summary to F1, the assertions on F1 fail for a reason unrelated to the change. Fix: State that F1 and F2 replace findings[0].summary in revising_critique().
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 4 (core tests.rs critic queue)

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot by reading the code. Its claims hold: `critic_brief` (planner.rs:185-210) and the `CriticInputs` literal (planning.rs:353-359) are as stated. `closing.plans` and `closing.critiques` are pushed together at planning.rs:483-484 and 312-313, the plan alone at 350, and a mechanical pass returns at 261 without pushing. `Closing::new()` is made once per run (mod.rs:1362) and `plan_round` is called once (mod.rs:1372). The plan record structs derive PartialEq (records/plan.rs). `critic_brief` and `CriticInputs` are used only where the dependents list says. The fixtures exist: `good_plan`, `critique_of` and the wrapper pattern in job_plan.rs; `planning_script` (which repeats the last queue entry), `bad_plan`, `revising_critique` and `prompts_of` in core tests.rs. The 900-token frame bound is at lib.rs:570. My byte count of critic.md (about 2216 to 2236) agrees with the plan's 2236, and the system-facts line 1056 = 310 + 746 matches. The approach is sound and the tests would fail on the old code. There is one major flaw in the prompt wording. Bullet B says "raise a major only on a part the brief lists as changed or new, or on a defect earlier rounds missed ... otherwise minor, even where a rule above says major". An earlier major that the planner ignored, leaving its part unchanged, is neither changed nor missed before. So the critic is told to report it as minor, and the plan can be accepted with that major still open. That defeats the point of the request, which is to check earlier findings were resolved. Bullet A says "name any that was not" but sets no severity. The rest are minor points about ambiguity and how far the tests can be checked.
